Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/14/Text/5] More specifically, the findings indicate that challenge appraisals positively predicted within-person changes and between-person mean differences in self-esteem (p < .001) and positive affect (p < .001) over time. Threat appraisals were unrelated to change in positive affect (p > .05), whereas it was negatively related to between-person average differences in self-esteem across the two seasons (p < .001). Challenge appraisals were inversely associated to within-person changes in negative affect (p < .05), whereas threat appraisals were unrelated to change in this outcome (p > .05).
